name: Endive Blue
lede: Endive Blue is a pale, cool grey that our library finds identical, on screen, to Light Blue Grey.

sections.title: Two names, one swatch
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature gives the swatch as plate XLIII, hue 49′′′, tone d, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 reads it as a pale blue, about 6.4 units from the block center; Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates the name itself to 1905 [1]. Our library carries the identical hex again under [[light-blue-grey]], at zero distance, despite "endive" naming a pale vegetable leaf, not a blue one [1][2].

The next distinct named color is [[pale-payne-s-grey]], about 3.7 units off, with [[deep-plumbago-blue]] and [[cadet-grey]] further out [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color, as photographed, appears in 411 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.73 percent, more common than 74 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 37 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.2 percent of that period's paintings, 1.6 times the overall rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light [3]. Its most devoted painter is Claude Monet, carrying it in 12 of 50 works here, 13.8 times the baseline for his museums [3]. The earliest match in the archive is a 1440 painting, 472 years before the name's 1912 record, so this is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a pigment identification, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

issues: Fixed: the field-notes paragraph (and the matching "field" object) invented a peak-decade stat (1930s/10.1%/5.4x+) that doesn't match any real field (the real pd field is 1840s/2.6%/1.9x and the century fact is the 1900s/2.2%/1.6x) and an earliest-match claim ("a 1119 illuminated manuscript", record year 1905) that doesn't match the real first-seen record (a 1440 painting, real record year 1912). The Claude Monet count was close but off (14 of 50, should be 12 of 50) and the presence count (445) didn't match the real count (411 as-photographed). Rewrote the paragraph directly from data/graph/fieldnotes for this slug; removed every unsupported claim rather than inventing a replacement for it.
